title: Machine learning helps select nickel(I)–phenyl complexes that insert CO₂ at room temperature
summary: The researchers calculated descriptors for 132 bidentate phosphine ligands, used k-means clustering to identify 21 candidate ligands, then applied DFT barrier calculations and human selection before synthesis. They isolated and characterized Ni(I)–phenyl complexes, including an X-ray-confirmed i-Pr-Xantphos complex. The i-Pr-Xantphos and dtbpf complexes underwent CO₂ insertion at room temperature in the reported experiments; nickel carboxylation was also tested. The study does not establish CO₂ insertion or Ni(I) chemistry generally as new; its result concerns bounded ligand selection/speciation.
ai_technology: Unsupervised k-means clustering of DFT-derived ligand descriptors
organization: Institute of Organic Chemistry, RWTH Aachen University; University of Jyväskylä

source_review.scope: Primary JACS full text, abstract, methods/results, chronology and affiliations.

evidence.tested: Synthesis, X-ray characterization, CO₂ insertion assays and catalytic carboxylation tests reported for selected Ni complexes.
evidence.unknown: Only representative ligands from predicted groups were experimentally evaluated; prior Ni(I)-CO₂ chemistry exists; results do not imply commercial carbon capture.
evidence.ai_role: Unsupervised clustering of computed descriptors identified a set of ligands to evaluate; DFT and researcher selection further narrowed candidates before synthesis and testing.
